titulo: Invoices and bills: the money passes through you
lead: Opening each supplier invoice, copying the number, due date, and amount into the accounts payable spreadsheet is one of the most boring tasks of the week. The agent can read and calculate, flag duplicate invoices, and flag totals that don’t match. The one thing it never does is pay: the list comes out as a draft, and the bank is yours to handle.
objetivo: have the agent read invoices and bills and make the accounts payable list, flagging duplicate invoices and totals that don’t match.

aprende.t: Pull the details from each invoice or bill
Check whether the line items add up to the total
Pick up the invoice that arrived twice

hero_alt: A person around 55 checks an amount on a paper invoice, beside bills, a calculator, and a laptop.

secoes.titulo: From a stack of invoices to a list of bills

nos.detalhe: For each invoice or bill, the agent pulls out the supplier, document number, date, due date, item amounts, and total. In the chat, attach the PDFs or paste the text; a photo works too if it’s clear.

It adds up the items and compares them with the printed total. If they don’t match, or a number is unreadable, the invoice is marked "doesn't match" and left off the list. It must not correct the amount on its own.
Has the same invoice number from the same supplier shown up before? It’s a duplicate: the supplier resent it, or it’s already in the spreadsheet. Flag it and skip it.
The accounts payable table, sorted by due date, with the week's total. It's a draft: you review it before copying it to the official spreadsheet.
You handle payments, approvals, and scheduling in the bank. The agent never gets your bank password or access to your financial system.

secoes.legenda: You always review money going out. The agent only takes care of typing and adding things up.

secoes.titulo: The sheet and four sample invoices
secoes.sub: The invoices are made up. Two have a problem on purpose.

blocos.conteudo:
Role: You are my accounts payable agent.
About me: [what the business does]; frequent suppliers and categories: [Lumberyard = raw materials; Accounting = services].
When: when I attach or paste the week’s invoices and bills and say "invoices".
Steps: 1) for each document, pull out the supplier, number, date, due date, items, and total; 2) add up the items and compare them with the printed total; 3) check whether the same supplier with the same number has already appeared in this batch or in the list of previously entered invoices I paste; 4) make a table: supplier, number, due date, total, category, status; 5) add up the week’s total using only invoices without problems.
Rules: only read, never change or delete anything; login screen = stop and call me; copy numbers exactly; if the sum doesn’t match or a number is unreadable, mark it "doesn't match" and leave it out of the total; duplicate invoice: mark it "duplicate" and leave it out of the total; never pay, approve, or schedule a payment; never ask for a bank password; everything is a draft for me to check; if you’re unsure, stop and ask.
Delivery: the table sorted by due date and, below it, the week’s total and the list of items left out, with the reason.
First task: run it now with the invoices I’m going to paste.

invoices

Document 1 · Invoice 4471 · Strong Pine Lumber · issued Oct 27 · due Nov 10
  MDF panels: 1,100.00 · shipping: 150.00 · TOTAL: 1,250.00

Document 2 · Invoice 5120 · Silva Hardware · issued Oct 28 · due Nov 12
  hinges: 480.00 · pulls: 320.00 · TOTAL: 900.00

Document 3 · Invoice 4471 · Strong Pine Lumber · issued Oct 27 · due Nov 10
  MDF panels: 1,100.00 · shipping: 150.00 · TOTAL: 1,250.00

Document 4 · Bill 311 · Rocha Accounting · due Nov 15
  November accounting fees · TOTAL: 650.00

abas.html:
• Invoice 4471 (Lumberyard): 1,250.00, due Nov 10, OK.
  • Bill 311 (Accounting): 650.00, due Nov 15, OK.
  • Invoice 5120 (Hardware): doesn't match. The items add up to 800.00, but the total says 900.00. Left out of the total.
  • Document 3: invoice 4471 duplicate. Left out of the total.
  • Week’s total: 1,900.00.

These calculations were done by hand using the example. Take invoice 5120 up with the supplier; the agent doesn’t decide which amount is correct.

In the my-agents/invoices folder, with the sheet in AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md), put the week’s PDFs in a week subfolder and run codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6-luna -s read-only -o bills.md "invoices: follow AGENTS.md using the files in the week folder".

If a PDF is a scanned image and the light model can’t read it, it should say "couldn’t read" (that’s the rule), and you can send it to the top model or type it in.

• Letting the agent "fix" the total: it can't know whether the line item or the total is wrong. You resolve it with the vendor.
  • Sending only the total, without the line items: without the line items, it has nothing to add up.
  • Giving it bank access "just to read the statement": that's outside this course's scope. Export the statement if you need to.

secoes.sub: Run the agent with the four sample invoices and paste the table it returned here. The page checks for the duplicate invoice, the one that doesn’t match, and the correct total for the week.

secoes.sub: Practice with the example, then with your invoices.

exercicios.texto: Create the "Accounts payable" Project with the sheet, paste the four sample invoices, and say "invoices". Paste the answer into the checker.
exercicios.pronto: the checker replies OK: 5120 marked as doesn't match, 4471 as duplicate, and total of 1,900.00.

exercicios.texto: Attach real invoices and bills from one week. Before copying them into your spreadsheet, check two totals on paper.
exercicios.pronto: the two checked totals match the table, and the agent hasn't paid any invoice.

exercicios.texto: Add your five most frequent vendors to the agent sheet, along with each one's category.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: On invoice 5120, the items add up to 800.00 and the printed total says 900.00. What should the agent do?
opcoes: Mark it as "doesn't match," leave it out of the total, and tell you.
Ask the vendor for a 100.00 discount to make up the difference.
perguntas.explica: The agent doesn't know where the error is: in an item or in the total. You handle it with the vendor. Its job is to find the difference and keep it out of the calculation.

perguntas.p: With the four sample invoices, what is the total due for the week?
perguntas.explica: Only the invoices without a problem count: 1,250.00 (4471) + 650.00 (bill 311) = 1,900.00. Invoice 5120 doesn't match, and document 3 is a duplicate of 4471. 4,050.00 is the sum of everything, without checking.

perguntas.p: Why should the invoice agent never get the bank password, not even "just to read"?
opcoes: Because the light model doesn't know how to use a bank website, and the top model would need a separate paid plan to do it.
Because the rule "money goes through you" means only you can pay and approve; you can read the statement by exporting it.
Because the bank blocks all AI access.
Because the password can only go in AGENTS.md.
perguntas.explica: Bank read access opens the door to everything else. An exported statement lets the agent read it without risk. The password doesn't go in the agent sheet, AGENTS.md, or the chat.

itens.texto: The agent extracts the details from each invoice and checks whether the items add up to the total.
Duplicates and items marked "doesn't match" stay out of the total, with the reason noted. You handle the issue.
The list comes out as a draft. You handle paying, approving, and scheduling.
